Launching a new warehouse is a major milestone, but what makes me most proud is the incredible teamwork behind it.

Today, we celebrate the opening of ID Logistics in Rugby; a significant investment in our future, our customers, and our continued growth. Facilities and infrastructure are important, but the real success story is the people who made it happen.

Over just 11 weeks, colleagues from across the business have come together with a shared goal; rolling up their sleeves, supporting one another, and demonstrating the commitment, collaboration and determination that define our culture. From planning and preparation to execution, every team and every individual played a part in making this launch happen on schedule.

Seeing so many people step outside their day-to-day roles to support the project has been truly inspiring. It is a powerful reminder that when we work together as one team, we can achieve extraordinary things.

# LPP Logistics Opens New Warehouse near Bucharest 

30 July 2026

LPP Logistics, the company that provides logistics for the Reserved, Cropp, House, Mohito and Sinsay brands, is expanding its operational capacities in South-Eastern Europe by opening a distribution center near Bucharest.

The unit, with an area of ​​56,000 sqm, serves the LPP Group stores in Romania, Bulgaria and Greece. An additional advantage of the location is its proximity to the port of Constanta, which streamlines the organization of deliveries by sea.

The launch of the new center also marks the completion of the reconstruction of the logistics infrastructure following the fire that occurred at the warehouse last year.

“The launch of the new distribution center just one year after the decommissioning of the previous warehouse demonstrates the operational efficiency of LPP Logistics and the ability of our team to quickly rebuild the infrastructure essential for business continuity. # Maersk Commits US$100m to New Hopedale Fulfillment Center, Advancing Integrated Logistics Push in the US Northeast

Maersk, the global integrator of container logistics operating across more than 130 countries, is deepening its footprint in North American contract logistics with a US$100m investment in a new fulfillment center in Hopedale, Massachusetts. The 617,000-square-foot facility is scheduled to open in late August 2026, positioning the company to strengthen fulfillment capacity for cargo owners across the region.

Built around the requirements of a single major e-commerce customer, the site will function as a central node in Maersk’s contract logistics network throughout the US Northeast. During peak periods, the center is engineered to process up to 330,000 units a day, a throughput enabled by advanced conveyor and sortation systems designed for high-volume, rapid-turnaround operations.

# Averitt expands logistics network with Jackson, Mississippi, facility

 August 27, 2026 

Less-than-truckload carrier Averitt said Thursday it has opened a 100,000-square-foot distribution and fulfillment facility in Jackson, Mississippi. The announcement follows other recent investments the carrier has made to its network.

The new warehouse is near central Mississippi’s major freight lanes of I-20 and I-55. The Mississippi Department of Transportation announced Tuesday a $400 million project to improve the roadways and bridges along these corridors. The plan also calls for rail upgrades.

Most national LTL carriers have nearby service centers and Averitt operates a 57-door LTL terminal next to the new facility. 

Cookeville, Tennessee-based Averitt’s latest addition will serve rail connections and provide service to ports in New Orleans and Mobile, Alabama. Customers will be able to flex the amount of space needed for seasonal and overflow inventory projects without committing to long-term contracts.

# Penske Logistics Debuts Multi-Client Warehouse in Brazil 

August 13, 2026

Penske Logistics South America has opened a new multi-client warehouse in Brazil. It is strategically located in Cajamar, in the São Paulo metropolitan region, near the Viracopos and Guarulhos international airports and the state’s major highways. The flexible operation will allow a company to increase its storage space and transportation capacity according to demand, meeting the needs of peak periods.

“Making this multi-client warehouse available in Brazil reinforces Penske’s commitment to always seeking innovations capable of meeting market demands,” noted Paulo Sarti, Penske Logistics managing director.

The warehouse has a total of 10,500 m² (with the possibility of expansion to 25,000 m²). The warehouse also earned a Golden Sustainability Seal, featuring water collection for reuse and LED lighting.

Penske Logistics has facilities concentrated in three strategic Brazil states: São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro and Paraná.
